slice: exploring: orienting with no brain of a human kind, flying, swimming, water-surface travel, sperm

items.sentence: A geodesic is a co-chaining a thing floats where a force acts on nothing, curving as relating curves, straight by relating's own terms.
items.text: A sea urchin sperm is swimming along a helix, radius about 8.4 µm, one winding about each 0.38 s, at about 200 µm/s; its own winding brings it a rising and falling of attractant about twice a second, and while the slower level is rising its helix is bending smoothly toward the gradient, and as the level is turning to falling it is making a sharp turn, in 9 of 10 cells watching; its sensing is coming from its own going on.

A larval zebrafish in a flow, with no sight of anything still, is reading the flow's slowing between its head and its tail through the sensing organs along its body; going from more gradient to less it is keeping its heading, and going from less to more it is making a strong turn with the flow's own rotating about its body.

items.sentence: A method co-chains geodesically, free-moving, adding nothing.
items.text: A dung beetle is rolling its ball in a straight line away from the dung pile, holding its line by sun, moon, the light's polarizing around them, and at night by the Milky Way's glow alone; under cloud its straight line is lost, and its sky cues outweigh landmarks nearby.

items.sentence: Both bothboth, one at a time, freeing sharing and testing receiving, and a method co-chains both sides with every observing.
items.text: A honeybee is flying through a narrow gap by evening the image speeds of its two eyes, setting its flight speed by holding image speed even, knowing distance by its summing image motion, and landing by holding a surface's image speed even, its own speed coming to stillness at touching.

items.sentence: A method co-chains between selves, and co-competencing is discovering with a same-existing-society's scale.
items.text: A water strider is standing on the surface, each foot in a small dimple, rowing with its middle legs and steering with its hind legs, vortices in pairs under the dimples moving it forward; its front legs are sensing the ripples of prey, and its kind is sharing its own surface waves in courtship and in holding a territory.

A whirligig beetle is finding still objects at the water surface, and whether it is sensing echoes of its own surface waves or the surface's curving around each object is still-possibling, the strongest test leaning to the curving.

A living self is orienting with no map and no measure apart from its own going on: its own winding, its two sides, its body along a flow, its sky, its surface, each changing it is observing a parity of now beside its prior, and each orienting a natural illustration of exploring from within a surface.
